Count the number of members in an ensemble

Source: R/C5.0.R, R/ObliqueForest.R, R/bart.R, and 9 more
num_ensemble_members.Rd

Ensembles of trees or rules, such as random forests or boosted models, contain multiple models. This generic returns how many there are. For most models this is the number of trees. For C5.0 models it is the number of boosting trials and, for Cubist models, the number of committees. For multiclass boosted models (e.g., from xgboost and lightgbm), the count is the total number of trees across all classes.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'C5.0'
num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ObliqueForest'
num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bart'
num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'catboost.Model'
num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cforest'
num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cubist'
num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'grf'
num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lgb.Booster'
num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'randomForest'
num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ranger'
num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'xgb.Booster'
num_ensemble_members(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A object

...

Other arguments passed to methods

Value

A single integer.

Details

The value is the largest index that can be passed to the tree (or committee) argument of methods such as extract_rules() and active_predictors().

Methods are only available for model classes that can be ensembles; single tree models (e.g., from rpart::rpart()) do not have a method.

Examples

if (rlang::is_installed("ranger")) {
  rf <- ranger::ranger(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars, num.trees = 10)
  num_ensemble_members(rf)
}
#> [1] 10
